The program

13 weeks. Three phases. One complete transformation.

SAAP is the only program that combines full scholarship strategy with hands-on technical bioinformatics training —
so you don't just sound research-ready, you actually are.

Phase 1 · Wks 1–3
Research Foundation
You begin with a real, mentorship-guided bioinformatics project. By the end of Week 3, you already have a completed analysis — before most applicants have even opened a terminal. Genomics workflows, sequencing technologies, public databases.
Phase 2 · Wks 4–10
Technical Bioinformatics Training
R for genomics. Linux command line. Bash scripting. RNA-Seq pipelines. Python from scratch. Biopython for sequence analysis. Capstone project on real biological data — the portfolio piece your future supervisor sees before they read your CV.
Phase 3 · Wks 11–13
Scholarship Strategy & Application Development
Global scholarship mapping across Canada, UK, Europe and beyond. The Dr. MBM SOP Framework. Essays for Commonwealth, Chevening, DAAD, Erasmus Mundus, Mastercard Foundation. CV rebuild. Cold email strategy. Expert review. Final submission-ready package.
PHASE 1 · WEEKS 1–3
Research Foundation
Week 1 Program Orientation & Bioinformatics Foundations
You learn how real research works — sequencing technologies, biological data formats, genomics workflows, and computational biology fundamentals. You also get introduced to the guided research project you'll be developing across the internship phase.
Week 2 Project Design & Data Analysis
You acquire real genomics datasets from public databases, begin preprocessing and exploratory analysis, and start developing your applied project under direct mentorship.
Week 3 Internship Project Completion
You complete, analyse, interpret, and present your first bioinformatics investigation. By the end of Week 3 you already have a completed research project — before most applicants have even opened a terminal.
PHASE 2 · WEEKS 4–10
Technical Bioinformatics Training
Week 4 R for Genomics Data Analysis
You learn R from the ground up — data importation, biological data structures, wrangling, cleaning, and visualisation of genomic datasets for exploratory analysis.
Week 5 Linux Environment Setup
You configure your Linux environment, learn the command line, navigate file systems, and understand exactly why Linux is the backbone of every serious bioinformatics pipeline.
Week 6 Bash Scripting & Biological Data Retrieval
You automate repetitive tasks, download biological datasets from repositories like NCBI, and manage bioinformatics workflows — all from the command line.
Week 7 RNA-Seq Workflow with Linux
You build a real transcriptomics pipeline — installing bioinformatics tools, preprocessing sequence data, running quality control, and automating workflows with Bash scripting.
Week 8 Python Programming Fundamentals
You learn Python from scratch — variables, data types, string manipulation, lists, dictionaries, tuples, and handling structured biological datasets with code.
Week 9 Python & Biopython for Bioinformatics
You go deeper — conditional statements, loops, functions, object-oriented programming, sequence handling with Biopython, biological sequence alignment, and genomic data analysis using Python-based tools.
Week 10 Capstone Bioinformatics Project
You apply everything — independently — to a full project in human health research, animal genetics, plant biology, or microbial genomics. This is your portfolio piece. This is what your future supervisor sees on GitHub before they ever read your CV.
PHASE 3 · WEEKS 11–13
Scholarship Strategy & Application Development
Week 11 Scholarship Strategy & Opportunity Mapping
You map the global scholarship landscape across Canada, Europe, the UK, and beyond. You learn exactly how selection criteria work, identify the universities and programs you're genuinely competitive for, and build a personalised scholarship search and application strategy.
Week 12 Scholarship Application Development
You write your Statement of Purpose using the Dr. MBM Framework. You craft essays for Commonwealth, Chevening, DAAD, Erasmus Mundus, and Mastercard Foundation scholarships. You rebuild your CV for scholarship committees. You learn how to find and cold email potential PhD supervisors — and get your drafts reviewed by mentors.
Week 13 Final Review & Application Packaging
Every essay reviewed. Every document polished. Every question answered. You leave with a complete, submission-ready scholarship application package — and the clarity to know exactly where to send it.
